name: Tracking Kerning And Line Spacing QC
use_when: A title, caption, or graphic feels cheap despite using an appropriate font.
Letters or lines feel too loose, too tight, or uneven at final size.
The agent is finishing a reusable text preset.
A CapCut social title, caption, or video-in-text word needs a premium tight-letter look.
avoid_when: The text has not yet been corrected for wording, hierarchy, or placement.
The typography will be read at very small size where tight spacing harms accessibility.
The platform or font renderer creates shimmer or aliasing with tight tracking.

timeline_pattern.pattern: lock_text_and_font -> check_line_breaks -> tune_tracking -> inspect_kerning_pairs -> tune_line_spacing -> preview_bright_and_dark_frames -> save_preset
timeline_pattern.tracking_rule: Slightly tightened tracking can feel more premium on large titles, but readability is the floor.
timeline_pattern.kerning_rule: Inspect large words for awkward gaps or collisions between specific letter pairs.
timeline_pattern.line_spacing_rule: Line spacing should group related lines without making them touch or feel disconnected.
timeline_pattern.preset_rule: Save spacing as a preset only after testing short, long, bright-background, and dark-background phrases.

motion.rule: Spacing must be checked again after scale, pop, typewriter, tracking, or camera motion.

keyframe_values.tracking_start: For display titles, start with very small tightening, around 1-4% or the nearest tool equivalent, then preview at final size.
keyframe_values.capcut_large_text: For large social title text in CapCut, values around -1 or -2 character spacing can work as a starting point when letters do not collide or shimmer.
keyframe_values.capcut_premium_text: Clean bold title fonts such as Fig Tree Bold can start around Character -1 in CapCut, then must be checked after compounding, masking, glow, or perspective effects.
keyframe_values.caption_tracking: Keep continuous captions near normal tracking unless a brand style has passed readability QC.
keyframe_values.line_height: Use compact but breathable line spacing; avoid stacked lines touching during pop or bounce motion.

captions.rule: Caption spacing should make the line easier to read; do not chase premium title spacing on subtitles.

color.rule: Tight spacing needs stronger contrast because thin gaps can disappear over busy backgrounds.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use drawtext line_spacing and font options where available; use ASS subtitles for more precise spacing and style control.
implementation.remotion: Store tracking, letterSpacing, lineHeight, maxLineWidth, and spacingQcStatus on text components.
implementation.blender: Use text object character spacing and line spacing controls, then inspect from the final camera distance.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Adjust Character spacing lightly, such as -1 for polished captions or -2 for large video-in-text words, then check large words manually and avoid over-tight continuous subtitles.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use Essential Graphics tracking, leading, and manual kerning where needed; recheck after scale or transform presets.

common_mistakes: Ignoring awkward gaps in big title words.
Using loose line spacing that breaks phrase unity.
Testing spacing only on one short word before saving a preset.
Copying -1 or -2 character spacing to small captions where it reduces accessibility.
Letting motion scale make clean spacing collide.
qc: Do letters avoid collisions at final size?
Do large title words have no obvious awkward gaps?
Do multi-line captions read as grouped phrases?
Does spacing survive the animation at its largest and smallest scale?
Has the spacing preset been tested on multiple phrase lengths?
